stories.title: Colliers Markets Senior Loan on DTLA’S EY Plaza
stories.excerpt: Colliers has launched the marketing of the senior loan secured by EY Plaza, the 41-story, 968,745-square-foot office tower at 725 S. Figueroa St. in Downtown Los Angeles, on behalf of the lender. The loan is held in a single-asset, single-borrower securitization, and the property is operated under a court-appointed receiver. Offers are due in October. The offering comes as Downtown Los Angeles office acquisition activity increasingly favors owner-users. Recent purchases by organizations, including Capital Group, Los Angeles County, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, Southwest Carpenters Pension Trust, and L.A. Care Health Plan, have shifted nearly five million square feet of inventory toward occupant ownership. “Buyers aren’t pricing Downtown Los Angeles as a submarket anymore. They’re underwriting each tower on its own floorplates, tenancy and owner-user potential,” said Sean Fulp, Vice Chair at Colliers. “That’s why two buildings a few blocks apart can trade at very different values.” Alongside Fulp, the Colliers investment sales team includes Executive Vice Presidents Todd Tydlaska and Mark Schuessler and Associate Vice Presidents Jordan Garcia and Blake Hammerstein. The leasing team includes Vice Chair Matt Heyn, Executive Vice President Ian Gilbert, and Senior Vice President Kurt Davis. The post Colliers Markets Senior Loan on DTLA’S EY Plaza appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: EY Plaza (41-story, 968K SF office tower, DTLA) loan marketed by Colliers; property in receivership.
DTLA office market shifting toward owner-user occupancy; five million SF recently purchased by Capital Group, LA County, LADWP, pension funds.
Buyers underwriting towers individually by floorplate, tenancy, owner-user potential—not pricing DTLA as unified submarket.
stories.summary: Colliers is marketing a senior loan secured by EY Plaza, a 41-story, 968,745-SF office tower in Downtown Los Angeles, with offers due in October. The property is under court-appointed receivership. Market activity increasingly favors owner-user purchases, with recent transactions by Capital Group, LA County, LA Department of Water and Power, Southwest Carpenters Pension Trust, and LA Care Health Plan shifting nearly five million square feet to occupant ownership. Buyers now underwrite individual towers by floorplate and tenancy rather than treating DTLA as a unified submarket.
stories.impact: DTLA office distress and fragmented pricing create minimal direct multifamily opportunity—office-to-residential conversion remains capital-intensive and entitlement-heavy. However, the shift toward owner-user occupancy and institutional capital consolidation in DTLA signals stabilization in the downtown core, which may anchor adjacent multifamily demand and stabilize rents in Court Square and related mixed-use submarkets over a 3–5 year horizon.

stories.title: New York People and Company News, Week of Sept. 18, 2026
stories.excerpt: Newmark has hired Susan Machtiger, a recognized expert in advising some of the largest companies in the world, as Executive Chairman, Newmark Consulting. In her role, Machtiger will work in close partnership with Dr. Yasmeen Coning to lead the consulting practice’s continued expansion into business strategy, people, purpose, place and brand, bringing these disciplines together to address the increasingly interconnected priorities shaping enterprise performance and growth. Rudin announced that Steven McKessey has joined the firm as Head of Design and Construction, overseeing Rudin’s 13.1-million-square-foot commercial and multifamily portfolio. A capital projects executive with more than two decades of experience spanning construction management and strategic consulting on large-scale projects, McKessey will direct capital planning, design and construction activities for all Rudin properties. LNL Capital has appointed Joel Tomlinson as Managing Partner to expand the Company’s structured debt and equity strategy within the single-tenant retail, industrial, and healthcare net lease space. Tomlinson brings over 25 years of industry experience to LNL Capital, having completed more than $15 billion in direct net lease transactions across public and non-traded REITs and alternative asset managers over the course of his career. He joins LNL Capital from Ares Management, where he served as Managing Director and was a founding member of the firm’s net lease strategy. KSR announced the launch of its new office leasing division, expanding the firm’s brokerage services to include landlord and tenant representation throughout the New York City market. The new division builds on KSR’s established investment sales, retail leasing, and debt advisory capabilities, completing its full-service brokerage model in response to growing demand from existing clients for office leasing expertise. stories.title: Avison Young Arranges $115M Fannie Mae DUS loan for Rockrose
stories.excerpt: Avison Young arranged a $115-million first mortgage loan on behalf of an affiliate of Rockrose Development for the Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2, a 301-unit, luxury residential property located at 43-14 Queens St. in Long Island Cit. The financing was provided by Fannie Mae through Wells Fargo Multifamily Capital as its DUS Lender. Avison Young’s Tri-State Debt and Equity Finance team led by Principals Scott Singer and Andy Singer, Executive Director Kevin Swartz and Senior Director Kathleen McSharry arranged the financing alongside Rockrose COO Richard Brancato and VP Jim Lerro. Wells Fargo’s team was led by Pete Cannava, Head of Multifamily Capital and Community Lending and Investment, Philip Maniscalco, Head of Production, Multifamily Capital, and Brian Antonuccio, Head of East Coast Production. “Long Island City remains one of the region’s most compelling multifamily markets, driven by strong residential demand, extraordinarily convenient transportation, and ongoing neighborhood growth,” said Scott Singer. “Phase 2 has further elevated Rockrose’s earlier Phase 1 of the Eagle Lofts Collection, bringing a unique set of amenities and adding to Rockrose’s impressive track record of developing and operating successful communities throughout New York City. Our teams are proud to have recently celebrated 50 years together, as well as adding to the many successful executions between Wells Fargo, Rockrose and the Singer team at Avison Young.” The post Avison Young Arranges $115M Fannie Mae DUS loan for Rockrose appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Rockrose secures $115M Fannie Mae DUS loan for Eagle Lofts Collection Phase 2, Long Island City (301 units, luxury).
Wells Fargo/Fannie Mae financing demonstrates continued agency liquidity for stabilized multifamily assets in strong rental markets.
Long Island City confirmed as compelling multifamily market: strong demand, transit access, ongoing neighborhood growth driving Phase 2 after Phase 1 (790 units).
stories.summary: Avison Young arranged a $115-million Fannie Mae DUS loan through Wells Fargo Multifamily Capital for Rockrose Development's Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2—a 301-unit luxury residential property at 43-14 Queens Street in Long Island City. The financing demonstrates continued agency appetite for stabilized multifamily in tight rental markets. Long Island City is characterized by strong residential demand, transit convenience, and ongoing neighborhood growth.
stories.impact: Agency lending availability and pricing remain favorable for newly stabilized multifamily assets in supply-constrained, high-demand submarkets like Long Island City. Rockrose's ability to execute Phase 2 (301 units) after Phase 1 (790 units) in the same location signals sustained investor confidence and rental absorption in the submarket; this validates ground acquisition and development pipeline expansion for TCR in Queens Court Square and adjacent waterfront corridors over the next 18–24 months.

stories.title: MassDevelopment Issues Bond to Assist Conversion of Former Convent to Seniors Housing
stories.excerpt: MassDevelopment issued a $7,760,000 tax-exempt bond on behalf of 207 E Street LLC, an affiliate of South Boston Neighborhood Development Corporation, to convert the vacant former St. Augustine’s convent at 207 E St. in South Boston into seniors housing. Eastern Bank purchased the tax-exempt bond, which helped the organization achieve a lower cost of capital. In addition to the tax-exempt bond, MassDevelopment assisted the Massachusetts Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities with approval of federal tax credits that will provide approximately $11.7 million in equity for the project. “Housing is essential to strong communities and a strong economy,” said Economic Development Secretary Eric Paley, chair of MassDevelopment’s Board of Directors. “By transforming the former St. Augustine’s convent into senior housing, we are carrying this historic property’s legacy forward while helping older adults remain rooted in the South Boston neighborhood they call home.” The post MassDevelopment Issues Bond to Assist Conversion of Former Convent to Seniors Housing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MassDevelopment issued $7.76M tax-exempt bond for conversion of former St. Augustine's convent to seniors housing, South Boston.
Project includes $11.7M in federal tax credits (LIHTC); Eastern Bank purchased tax-exempt bond to reduce capital cost.
South Boston adaptive reuse signals demand for age-restricted/seniors housing; policy/financial support aligns with demographic aging.
stories.summary: MassDevelopment issued a $7.76-million tax-exempt bond on behalf of South Boston Neighborhood Development Corporation to convert the vacant St. Augustine's convent at 207 E Street into seniors housing. The project secured approximately $11.7 million in federal low-income housing tax credits. Eastern Bank's purchase of the bond provided favorable financing terms.
stories.impact: Tax-exempt financing and LIHTC availability for seniors conversions in established urban neighborhoods like South Boston demonstrate sustained capital access and policy support for age-restricted housing. For TCR, this underscores the Boston submarket's tolerance for adaptive reuse and mixed-income seniors products; however, multifamily developers should note that available downtown conversion sites may face competing demand from seniors operators and public-private partnerships, potentially elevating land/building acquisition costs.

stories.title: Beer-Importing Holterbosch Family Offloads LIC Warehouse for $95M
stories.excerpt: The Holterbosch family, former owners of a German beer importing and distribution business, has sold a Long Island City, Queens, warehouse a decade after the death of its patriarch. Dallas-based Ground Lease REIT, an affiliate of commercial real estate private equity firm Montgomery Street Partners, bought the property at 10-01 45th Road on the Long Island City waterfront for $95 million, according to a deed filing in property records made public Thursday. The Holterbosch clan has held the property since about 1968, public records indicate, despite the death of H. Dieter Holterbosch in 2016 at age 95. The company is named Hans Holterbosch Inc. and honors its founder who died in 1960. It is not clear if the company, once a major importer and distributor of Lowenbrau beer, is still active. Dieter’s daughter Heidi, who seems to have been his only survivor, signed the paperwork for the deed transfer to Ground Lease REIT. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. The Holterbosch family, which lists an office address at 375 Park Avenue, could not be reached for comment, while Ground Lease REIT did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The property along Vernon Boulevard is just feet from the Eleventh Street Basin inlet of the East River, which probably served as a logistical benefit in the past, and could also offer Ground Lease REIT development opportunities as the neighborhood continues to transform. In 2017, Heidi Holterbosch was looking for a buyer for an 8-acre site hugging Newtown Creek at 55-01 Second Street, which had been rezoned as residential as the city prepared for the redevelopment of Hunters Point South. Listed for $350 million, that site was eventually razed by TF Cornerstone to make way for housing developments in 2021. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Holterbosch family sold Long Island City warehouse (10-01 45th Road) to Ground Lease REIT affiliate for $95M; property held since ~1968.
Ground Lease REIT (Montgomery Street Partners affiliate) acquired asset; suggests industrial/ground-lease portfolio consolidation in LIC waterfront.
Long Island City warehouse market remains competitive; generational hold-ups releasing assets to institutional capital.
stories.summary: The Holterbosch family, former owners of a German beer importing business, sold a Long Island City warehouse at 10-01 45th Road on the waterfront to Ground Lease REIT (an affiliate of Montgomery Street Partners) for $95 million. The property had been held by the family since approximately 1968. The deed transfer was signed by Heidi Holterbosch, likely the patriarch's surviving heir.
stories.impact: LIC waterfront industrial asset sales to ground-lease specialists signal rising land valuations and institutional capital consolidation in the submarket. For multifamily developers, this raises acquisition costs for adjacent LIC waterfront sites and may increase competition for trophy development land; however, it also reinforces Long Island City's status as a high-value, capital-intensive submarket with strong underlying demand, validating luxury multifamily product in Court Square and Hunters Point South.

stories.title: Juanita’s Foods to Consolidate L.A. Production at 120K-SF Facility
stories.excerpt: An 80-year-old food manufacturer is consolidating its Southern California operations into a new 120,000-square-foot facility in Santa Fe Springs, in the first deal backed by a recently formed alliance of four Los Angeles County industrial cities. Juanita’s Foods will move production from its longtime Wilmington plant to 13100 Arctic Circle in Santa Fe Springs. The deal includes an incentives agreement as well as expedited permitting via the four-city partnership. Records show LBA Logistics acquired the facility in December 2019. The cities of Commerce, Santa Fe Springs, Vernon and the City of Industry formed the Big 4 partnership in October 2025 as an economic-development coalition to coordinate investment attraction rather than compete for the same industrial employers. Together, the four cities offer about 250 million square feet of industrial space, and host more than 5,000 businesses with a workforce of about 200,000. The Big 4 cities estimate their combined industrial base generates roughly $33 billion in economic activity. “This is what becomes possible when cities stop looking at economic development as a competition and start looking at it as a regional opportunity,” Santa Fe Springs City Manager René Bobadilla said in a statement. Juanita’s said it considered locations around the country before deciding to remain in Southern California. “We conducted an exhaustive nationwide search before deciding where Juanita’s Foods would build its next chapter,” Chief Operating Officer Jody Jordan said. He cited Santa Fe Springs’ approach to business and the incentive package as key factors in the decision. LBA Logistics did not immediately return a request for comment. In May 2025, Juanita’s Foods sold a majority stake to Miami-based private equity firm Apex Capital as part of the founding De La Torre family’s estate planning. The family retained a minority interest and remains involved in operations. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.co
bullets: Juanita's Foods consolidating SoCal operations: moving from Wilmington to 120K-SF facility in Santa Fe Springs (13100 Arctic Circle).
Big 4 city partnership (Commerce, Santa Fe Springs, Vernon, City of Industry) formed Oct 2025 to attract/retain industrial employers; coordinated incentives and expedited permitting.
Big 4 controls 250M SF industrial space, 5K+ businesses, 200K-person workforce; $33B annual economic activity—regional employment hub stabilization.
stories.summary: Juanita's Foods, an 80-year-old food manufacturer, is consolidating its Southern California production into a new 120,000-square-foot facility in Santa Fe Springs, marking the first deal under a newly formed Big 4 city partnership (Commerce, Santa Fe Springs, Vernon, City of Industry). The alliance, launched in October 2025, provides incentives and expedited permitting to coordinate industrial recruitment. The four cities collectively control approximately 250 million square feet of industrial space, host 5,000+ businesses, employ 200,000 workers, and generate roughly $33 billion in annual economic activity.
stories.impact: Industrial consolidation and employer coordination in LA County's Big 4 corridor stabilizes regional employment and logistics hub functionality, supporting sustained warehouse/industrial leasing and supporting services demand. For multifamily developers, this reinforces the feasibility of Class B/C apartment development in adjacent residential submarkets (Santa Fe Springs, Vernon periphery) where workforce housing demand remains underserved and rents remain accessible; consider ground acquisition in transit-accessible residential pockets within 3–5 miles of Big 4 nodes.

stories.title: Knighthead Lends $63M or Doral, Fla., Industrial Portfolio Buy
stories.excerpt: Midtown Capital Partners has sealed $62.92 million of acquisition financing to fund its purchase of 13 urban-infill, small-bay industrial assets in Doral, Fla., Commercial Observer has learned. Knighthead Funding provided the loan for Midtown’s $86 million off-market acquisition of the 290,000-square-foot portfolio spanning 13.33 acres, according to the lender. Midtown purchased the properties from Wes Realty in August at a near-record industrial sales price for Miami-Dade County, The Real Deal previously reported. The 13 properties were developed and assembled over the last 30 years, according to Knighthead, which originated the deal with a team led by Jonathan Daniel, Alexandra Wiggins and Joseph Marraccini. “This transaction epitomizes what we look for when financing a deal — an attractive collection of assets with significant upside in an excellent infill location,” Wiggins, vice president at Knighthead Funding, said in a statement. The properties, which are located west of Miami within a mile of Miami International Airport, benefit from strong demand for small-bay industrial properties in South Florida, where vacancy rates are below 3 percent, according to Knighthead. Arrow Real Estate Advisors arranged the debt with a team consisting of Morris Betesh, Morris Dabbah and Zach Strauss. “Urban-infill portfolios like this come around once in a lifetime,” Betesh, founder and managing partner at Arrow, said in a statement. “We’ve seen the small-bay industrial sector mature significantly over the last several years, and this acquisition, along with the capital markets’ reception to the transaction, is another indication of how increasingly institutional the asset class has become.” Midtown Capital Partners did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Knighthead Funding arranged $62.92M acquisition loan for Midtown Capital Partners' purchase of 13-asset industrial portfolio in Doral, Fla. (290K SF).
Midtown acquired $86M portfolio of small-bay, infill industrial assets west of Miami, near Miami International Airport; near-record Miami-Dade industrial pricing.
Portfolio locations within 1 mile of MIA provide strategic logistics advantage; Knighthead highlighted significant upside potential.
stories.summary: Knighthead Funding provided $62.92 million in acquisition financing for Midtown Capital Partners' purchase of a 13-property industrial portfolio in Doral, Florida. The $86-million off-market acquisition includes 290,000 square feet of small-bay, infill industrial assets spanning 13.33 acres. The properties are located west of Miami within one mile of Miami International Airport and were developed and assembled over 30 years.
stories.impact: Miami-Dade industrial acquisition at near-record pricing and institutional lender appetite (Knighthead's backing) signal sustained capital availability for supply-constrained, logistics-adjacent industrial assets near MIA. For multifamily developers, this reflects strong logistics and e-commerce employment growth in the Miami metro, validating workforce housing demand in Doral, Wynwood, Allapattah, and adjacent neighborhoods; consider multifamily development pipelines targeting essential worker and middle-income segments near emerging industrial/logistics clusters.

stories.title: Ares Management, PSP Investments Form $2.4B U.S. Logistics Partnership
stories.excerpt: Ares Management is diving deeper into the waters of U.S. logistics. The $670 billion private equity powerhouse announced Wednesday that it has formed a joint venture with Canada’s Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments) to invest up to $2.4 billion into the development and acquisition of U.S. logistics facilities. Ares plans to combine its vertically integrated logistics real estate platform, Marq Logistics, with PSP’s scaled capital to invest into “high-conviction markets” and “strategically placed logistics facilities,” according to a release. Dave Fazekas, head of North America logistics at Ares Real Estate, noted in a statement that his firm was motivated to invest into domestic logistics hubs due to resurgent onshoring trends, growth of digital infrastructure construction, and the economy’s ongoing reliance on e-commerce. “We are proud to expand Ares’ long-standing relationship with PSP Investments as we leverage our collective scale and experience to identify compelling deployment opportunities and deliver value for tenants, communities and investors,” he said. The joint venture already plans to invest in a 5.2 million-square-foot seed portfolio of 14 assets in California, Texas and New Jersey. Laurence Bastien, managing director of real estate investments for the Americas at PSP Investments, emphasized in a statement that the U.S. logistics sector is currently defined by “durable demand drivers and structurally constrained supply,” and the partnership with Ares provides his firm with an operating platform that will “drive value at the asset level.” “Best-in-class operators, in sectors where our conviction is strongest — that is what our real estate strategy is built around, and this joint venture has both,” added Bastien. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ares Management and PSP Investments (Canada) form $2.4B U.S. logistics joint venture; combined with Ares' Marq Logistics platform.
Motivation: onshoring trends, digital infrastructure growth, sustained e-commerce reliance; high-conviction market selection and strategic facility placement.
$670B AUM Ares + major pension capital signals institutional conviction in U.S. industrial logistics secular trends.
stories.summary: Ares Management announced a joint venture with Canada's Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments) to invest up to $2.4 billion into U.S. logistics facility development and acquisition. The partnership combines Ares' vertically integrated Marq Logistics platform with PSP's scaled capital to target high-conviction markets and strategically positioned facilities. Investment drivers include onshoring, digital infrastructure growth, and sustained e-commerce demand.
stories.impact: Mega-fund capital allocation ($2.4B) into domestic logistics development signals prolonged capital availability, rising land/development costs, and institutional competition for infill industrial sites in major metros. For multifamily developers, this accelerates land cost inflation in logistics-adjacent submarkets (Inland Empire, Atlanta Flex Corridor, Dallas DFW, Charlotte) and may constrain multifamily ground availability; however, it validates long-term logistics-hub employment growth and workforce housing demand in these regions over a 5–10 year horizon.

stories.title: Wells Fargo Refis Long Island City Apartments With $115M Fannie Mae Loan
stories.excerpt: An affiliate of Rockrose Development has secured $115 million of agency-backed debt to refinance a newly completed multifamily complex in Long Island City, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. Wells Fargo Multifamily Capital closed the Fannie Mae-backed loan for Rockrose’s 301-unit Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2, which opened last year in Long Island City’s Court Square neighborhood. The 19-story building on 43-14 Queens Street shares a lobby and amenities with Rockrose’s adjacent 790-unit Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 1 tower. Avison Young negotiated the debt with a tri-state debt and equity finance team consisting of Scott Singer, Andy Singer, Kevin Swartz and Kathleen McSharry. “Long Island City remains one of the region’s most compelling multifamily markets, driven by strong residential demand, extraordinarily convenient transportation, and ongoing neighborhood growth,” Scott Singer, principal at Avison Young, said in a statement. “Phase 2 has further elevated Rockrose’s earlier Phase 1 of the Eagle Lofts Collection.” Seventy percent of apartments at Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2 are market rate with 30 percent of the units designated as affordable housing. The property’s amenities include a spa with saunas, a bowling alley, a golf simulator and a rooftop pool. Wells Fargo originated the loan with a team led by Pete Cannava, head of multifamily capital and community lending and Investment; Philip Maniscalco, head of production for multifamily capital; and Brian Antonuccio, head of East Coast production. “With 301 new residences, nearly a third of them affordable, Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2 meaningfully expands housing access in Long Island City,” Maniscalco said in a statement. Richard Brancato, chief operating officer at Rockrose, said in a statement, the transaction “reflects the strength” of its “long-standing relationships” with Wells Fargo and Avison Young. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Rockrose Development refinances Eagle Lofts Phase 2 (301 units, Long Island City) with $115M Fannie Mae loan via Wells Fargo; 19-story, Court Square.
Asset completed and recently opened; shares lobby/amenities with adjacent Phase 1 (790 units); total 1,091-unit campus in LIC.
Agency refinance reflects strong underwriting, stabilized occupancy, rental growth in high-demand LIC market; institutional lender confidence.
stories.summary: Rockrose Development secured $115 million in agency-backed refinancing through Wells Fargo Multifamily Capital for Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2—a newly completed, 301-unit luxury apartment building at 43-14 Queens Street in Long Island City. The 19-story building shares a lobby and amenities with the adjacent 790-unit Phase 1 tower, creating a 1,091-unit campus. The refinance was negotiated by Avison Young's tri-state debt and equity team.
stories.impact: Rapid stabilization and agency refinance of a 301-unit new-delivery asset in Long Island City validates strong rental demand, absorption velocity, and rent growth in the Court Square submarket. For TCR, this confirms LIC's multifamily pipeline feasibility and supports acquisition/development of additional trophy-quality sites in the waterfront corridor; refinance velocity and favorable terms also signal continued Fannie Mae appetite for Class A stabilized multifamily in supply-constrained, transit-rich East Coast metros.
